name: Multi-tenant SaaS on Postgres
summary: One application serving many customer organisations, isolated with row-level security in Postgres, with billing, organisation roles and an audit log from the start. Built on a Next.js front end and a NestJS API.

fitsWhen.says: customers will ask for SOC 2 or GDPR evidence

frontend.why: Marketing pages rendered on the server and the app behind sign-in in one project.

backend.why: Guards and modules make the tenant check a rule every route passes through.

database.why: Row-level security enforces the tenant boundary in the database itself.

queue.why: Emails, webhooks to customers, billing sync.

auth.why: Organisations, invitations and enterprise SSO without building them.

observability.why: Every trace tagged with the tenant id.

testing.why: Tests that prove one tenant cannot see another's data.

hosting.why: Room to add per-region data residency later.

services.name: api
responsibilities: Sets the tenant for each transaction

dataStores.name: db
dataStores.purpose: Every tenant table has tenant_id and a row-level security policy

environments.name: dev
environments.hosting: docker compose with Postgres and Redis

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: A copy of production for checking a release
environments.hosting: A staging environment with seeded test tenants

environments.name: prod
environments.hosting: Production with point-in-time recovery for Postgres

stages.name: migrations
stages.does: Apply migrations to a copy of the schema

stages.name: deploy
stages.does: Staging on main, prod on tags

notes: Backups and restore tested every quarter

security.auth: Organisation-scoped sessions; the API sets the tenant in the database session for RLS
security.secrets: Cloud secret manager; per-tenant webhook secrets encrypted
notes: Validate every input at the API boundary and return typed errors, never stack traces.
Parameterised queries only (the ORM), so no SQL is built from strings.
Set secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies or short-lived tokens; rate-limit sign-in.
Check authorisation on every endpoint on the server, not only in the UI (OWASP A01 Broken Access Control).
Row-level security as the second lock behind the application check
An audit log of who changed what, per tenant

folderLayout:
apps/web/
apps/api/
  src/tenancy/
  src/audit/
  prisma/
packages/shared/
conventions: Every table has tenant_id; every query runs with the tenant set
Isolation tests are part of every feature's tests
Nothing is shared across tenants except the catalogue

adrs.title: Shared database with row-level security
adrs.decision: All tenants share one database; Postgres RLS enforces the boundary.
adrs.why: Cheaper and simpler than a database per tenant, and a missed WHERE clause cannot leak data.

adrs.title: Bought identity
adrs.decision: Organisations, invitations and SSO come from Clerk.
adrs.why: Enterprise SSO is expected by business buyers and costly to build.

repos.label: app
repos.layout: An npm workspace with apps/web and apps/api

files.template: How tenancy works, how to run it, and how to add a tenant-scoped table.
Reads the organisation from the verified session and sets it for the request.
An Organization model and one tenant-scoped example model with tenantId.
Enables row-level security on the example table with a policy on current_setting('app.tenant_id').
Lint, test and a migration dry run.
